scope: independent bridge transport source review, no runtime/visual review

verified_properties: Race: stop lane queues an authenticated observe/drive_step/trace_dispatch only when _pending is false and no queued peer exists; otherwise replies busy. Promotion happens only when _peer == null, at the top of _process, after _poll_queued_peer and _poll_stop_peer, so a primary that closed in frame N is replaced by the queued peer in frame N+1 and dispatched in that same frame (buffer already holds the newline, count<=0 early-return is bypassed).

One command owner: promoted request re-runs the full primary validator (token, tool type, args type, one_request_required, size) and dispatches once; _finish only replies when _pending, which the queued request never sets while waiting. Cancel paths (disconnect/send failure) only fire for was_pending on the primary, never for a queued peer.

Buffer aliasing: PackedByteArray assignments copy by value; each move (_stop_buffer->_queued_buffer->_buffer) is followed by resetting the source to a new PackedByteArray, so _close_stop/_close_queued/_close clear() calls cannot alias.
Timeout: queue expires after 5 s measured from _stop_accepted_at (so stop-lane read time counts), promoted primary inherits that accept time against the 15 s primary limit. Both bounded, no retry.
Disconnect: _poll_queued_peer polls status each frame and drops the peer without touching loop state; comment is accurate since nothing executed.

Stop safety: after queueing, _stop_peer is nulled immediately so the next connection enters the stop lane; Stop runs cancel() which bumps control_generation and clears enabled, so a later promoted drive_step/trace_dispatch/observe fails agent_not_ready/stale_dispatch/agent_disabled through the normal validators. verify_bridge_race asserts exactly this (stale_dispatch, stop < 1 s).
operation_finished binding unchanged (connected once in start(), _finish gated on _pending); loop, client, provider, UI, physics, thresholds untouched. No token or request body is logged or echoed.
remaining_limits: Expanded observe/drive/queuedStop regression is still running; not claimed as passed.

Queue expiry closes the queued connection silently (no NDJSON error). Client surfaces a generic connection-closed DesktopError, consistent with no-retry policy but less diagnosable than a 'busy' reply.

A long-running primary actor (drive_step up to ~14 s with settling) can outlast the 5 s queue window, so an actor arriving on the stop lane during a monitor-held primary then primary-pending sequence is dropped rather than served. Acceptable under one-owner rule; noted for operators.
Only one queued slot; a third concurrent connection during a held primary with a queued actor is not accepted by any lane until one frees (pre-existing single-stop-lane behavior).

Promoted request inherits the stop-lane 4096-byte bound, so actor requests larger than 4 KiB arriving on the secondary lane are closed, while the same request on the primary lane allows 1 MiB. Current client payloads are well under 4 KiB.

coordinator_observed: Expanded actual transport paths passed after review dispatch; queued actor frees Stop lane, observed32ms Stop and stale_dispatch for queuedreceipt.
